attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (RHEL 9) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, protecting it from the kernel OOM killer. Verified this under a real memory-exhaustion event: launched an unprotected memory-hog process that drove the system out of memory; the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the hog (oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api (oom_score_adj=-1000) continued serving /health and /inventory throughout with zero restarts. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, issued a native systemd reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed a changed boot_id proving an actual restart, and verified inventory-api auto-started (enabled unit), retained its OOM protection, and served requests correctly post-reboot.
